study.title: Evaluation of stenoses using AI video models applied to coronary angiography

imaging.modality_detail: Coronary angiography (CAG) X-ray videos in DICOM format, 512x512 pixels
imaging.territory_detail: Left and right coronary arteries (11 epicardial coronary artery segments)
imaging.frames_per_sequence: 24 frames centered around the reference area used as model input

public_dataset_used.detail: ARCADE public dataset (1200 X-ray CAG images) used as Dataset C for segmentation training/testing

data_released.detail: Model weights released; release of own data not reported

annotation.annotator_expertise: Interventional cardiologists with over 10 years of experience (Dataset B); main labels from clinical reports; QCA by trained technicians supervised by an expert physician (Dataset D)
annotation.inter_rater_value: Clinical reports vs expert consensus: MAE 21.00% (95% CI 20.20-21.76), r 0.5000

task.task_description: End-to-end video pipeline (DeepCoro) that registers stenosis regions across frames, segments 11 coronary artery segments, assigns stenoses to segments, and predicts continuous stenosis percentage and severe stenosis (>=70%) classification with a Swin3D video transformer.
task.clinical_application: Automated, standardized assessment of coronary artery disease stenosis severity from coronary angiography videos

temporal_evidence.quote: uses a modified version of the Swin3D[27] architecture, a state-of-the-art video classification transformer model

method.pretraining: Swin3D pretrained on Kinetics400 and ImageNetV1

evaluation.external_validation_detail: Authors call Dataset D (MHI QCA Core Lab, RCT angiograms) 'external validation', but the model was fine-tuned on its training split at the same institution

G1.quote: Direct comparisons between DeepCoro and other models in existing literature present challenges, primarily due to the unique and extensive dataset that our approach used

G2.quote: This dataset provided an ideal setting to evaluate DeepCoro adaptability to different clinical contexts

G3.quote: rely on static images instead of dynamic videos, potentially missing critical information that clinicians frequently derive from video analysis

G5.quote: these performances can be improved by annotating more data

G6.quote: conducting a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to compare revascularization decisions based on AI-assisted CAG interpretations versus traditional methods will be key in understanding DeepCoro

G9.quote: DeepCoro tends to underestimate stenosis severity reflecting the underlying stenosis distribution, likely due to the high prevalence of non-severe stenoses in the training dataset

other_limitations: Training/testing labels based on clinician visual interpretation that may not match true stenosis
Side branches and CABG patients excluded
Processing time of 62.60 s per video may hinder clinical use
Compounding error across multiple sequential algorithms
future_work: RCT comparing AI-assisted versus traditional revascularization decisions with FFR testing
Fine-tune for calcium estimation, vulnerable plaque identification or physiological impact of stenoses
Detect stenoses in complex coronary segments and side branches
Speed up processing via larger batch sizes and parallel computing
Large-scale datasets with objective QCA measures
